questions.question: Checkout p95 rises during a promotion, and the database connection-pool wait time rises at the same time. Which is the strongest next step?
options: Increase the caller timeout
Measure the pool's arrival rate, completion rate, and database headroom before changing capacity or offered work
Add more CPU to every API instance
Ignore p95 because average CPU is low
questions.explanation: Pool wait on the critical path points to a bounded shared resource. Confirm its demand and service capacity before choosing a targeted intervention.

questions.question: A query returns 50 rows but its execution plan examines millions. What should the team investigate before scaling application workers?
options: The query predicates, ordering, plan, buffers, and a selective index or rewrite
Only the browser bundle size
A larger retry budget
Whether the cache TTL can be infinite
questions.explanation: Rows examined versus rows returned is evidence of inefficient data access. Application workers cannot remove a scan or lock wait inside the database.

questions.question: A service receives 60,000 requests per second and cache hits fall from 92% to 76%. How many requests per second now reach the authoritative store?
questions.explanation: A 76% hit rate leaves 24% as misses. 60,000 x 0.24 = 14,400 requests per second to the authoritative store.

questions.question: Why can increasing a downstream timeout make a performance incident worse?
options: It always reduces cache hits
It lets requests hold threads, sockets, and pool slots longer without adding completion capacity
It prevents all retries
It makes an index unusable
questions.explanation: A longer timeout can hide immediate errors while more waiting work consumes the same constrained resources. It is not additional service capacity.

questions.question: A fulfillment queue is aging, but checkout latency and database pool wait remain healthy. Which response best protects the user-facing path?
options: Make checkout wait until every fulfillment job completes
Measure worker completion and downstream headroom, then add safe consumer capacity or throttle non-critical work
Remove the durable queue
Serve stale account balances to reduce traffic
questions.explanation: The asynchronous worker path is constrained, not checkout. Keep the durable user action independent while addressing the queue's arrival and completion rates.

questions.question: What makes an optimization experiment complete?
options: A local benchmark is faster
A favorite technique was deployed
The same representative workload improves the user-visible target without unacceptable correctness, reliability, or cost regressions
CPU utilization is lower on one server
questions.explanation: Performance work must prove an end-to-end improvement under representative load and make the trade-offs visible. A single local metric is insufficient.
